items.description: Family Promise assists families dealing with homelessness through multiple programs: The Hospitality Center provides temporary shelter for up to six families (20 people). The Hospitality Network rotates congregations for lodging and case management. Pathway to Diversion houses families 7–14 days. Pathway to Housing provides rapid rehousing with case management and financial assistance. Pathway to Independence connects families with community supports. The Hope Center provides shelter and case management.
items.eligibility: Families experiencing homelessness
items.notes: Call for street address. Multiple program tracks available.

items.title: Friendship House
items.summary: Transitional housing combining subsidized housing with holistic programming for adults recovering from substance abuse, domestic violence, or incarceration. Multiple houses across Wilmington for men and women.

contentSource.name: FIRST Community Services Directory — Delaware DSCYF

items.description: A Transitional Housing Program for people recovering from substance abuse, domestic violence, or incarceration who need additional time to achieve self-sufficient housing. Combines subsidized housing with holistic programming. Women's houses: Epiphany, Jane Ashford, Patterson, Palmer I & II, and Elizabeth House. Men's houses: Clark, Criswell, Corner, Daughtry, and Burton House. Residents move to a new house as they progress through stages.
items.eligibility: Adults recovering from substance abuse, domestic violence, or incarceration
items.notes: Multiple house locations across Wilmington. Call for placement.

items.summary: Short-term emergency motel placement for displaced individuals. Referrals accepted from social service agencies, schools, and hospitals. One-week stay, once per calendar year.

contentSource.name: FIRST Community Services Directory — Delaware DSCYF

items.description: Provides short-term emergency housing for individuals in need or displaced persons. Referrals accepted from social service agencies, schools, hospitals, prison outreach, and churches for placement in approved motels. Duration is usually one week. items.eligibility: Foster care and unaccompanied youth ages 16–23, including LGBTQ+ youth
items.notes: Ages 16–23 only.

items.title: Wilmington Housing Authority - Housing Choice Vouchers
items.summary: Federal housing vouchers helping eligible low-income residents pay rent in the community. Waitlist opens periodically — keep contact information current. WHA manages 1,976 vouchers.

contentSource.name: FIRST Community Services Directory — Delaware DSCYF

items.organization: Wilmington Housing Authority - Housing Choice Vouchers
items.description: Housing Choice Vouchers can be used in public housing units or toward rental assistance in the community. Eligible households include those with disabilities and elderly persons with income not exceeding 80% of local median income. The voucher pays a portion of rent; the resident pays the remainder. Vouchers are transferrable to other jurisdictions. Waitlists are only open during certain times of the year.
items.eligibility: Income at or below 80% of local median income; includes elderly and disabled persons
items.notes: Waitlist opens periodically. Keep contact information current. 1,976 total vouchers managed.

items.eligibility: Income at or below 80% of local median income; includes elderly and disabled persons
items.notes: Waitlist opens periodically. Keep contact information current.

items.summary: Transitional and rapid re-housing for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, and dating violence, with wraparound case management and financial assistance toward stable permanent housing.

contentSource.name: FIRST Community Services Directory — Delaware DSCYF

items.organization: YWCA Delaware - SCHE Joint Transitional Housing and Rapid Re-housing
items.description: YWCA Delaware's SCHE (Safe, Compassion, Heal, Empower) program offers survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, and dating violence personalized service plans to achieve housing stability. Services include community housing, case management, food access, wellness workshops, clothing, workforce readiness, medical/legal accompaniment, financial assistance, financial coaching, therapeutic services, and transportation.
items.eligibility: Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, or dating violence
items.notes: Call for intake. No fixed public address.

updates.title: Know Your Rights: Eviction Prevention Info Session
updates.summary: Free legal-aid info session covering tenant rights, eviction defenses, and emergency rental assistance.

updates.title: What is the eviction notice period in Delaware?
updates.summary: 5 days for nonpayment of rent, 7 days for lease violations, 60 days for no-cause termination.

updates.title: What can I do if my landlord won't return my security deposit?
updates.summary: Delaware law gives landlords 20 days to return a deposit or provide an itemized list of deductions.

updates.title: How much notice does my landlord have to give before eviction?
updates.summary: Notice periods depend on the reason for eviction — from 5 days for nonpayment up to 60 days for no-cause termination of a year-to-year lease.

updates.title: Delaware raises income threshold for Emergency Assistance eligibility
